core.title: Type every appendix as one of the six recognized appendix types
core.given: You are creating a plan artifact (the stack's plan-artifact kinds, per the profile) and have supplementary content (designs, data, docs, diagrams, recordings) attached or to attach as an appendix.
core.when: You name, classify, or read an appendix artifact.
core.then: Classify it as exactly one of the six recognized appendix types (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video), using a file extension from that type's allowed extension list in the profile.
prefer: mockup [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: visual designs, UI mockups, wireframes, prototypes; informs component structure and harness selection. Use cases: UI screen designs → component structure during feature decomposition; user flow diagrams → fine-grained plan item (per the profile) decomposition and when/must/then statements; visual states (loading, error, success) → harness selection (visual, e2e); responsive variants (mobile, tablet, desktop) → acceptance criteria.

spreadsheet [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: data models, calculations, business rules, requirements matrices; informs the domain model and acceptance criteria. Use cases: complex pricing/tax calculation logic → domain model and business rules; data validation rules → acceptance criteria; requirement traceability matrices → feature clustering; test data sets → acceptance given/when sections.

document [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: specifications, research findings, technical guides, product requirement documents; informs coarse plan artifact (per the profile) description and component contracts. Use cases: product requirements documents → coarse plan artifact description and scope; technical specifications → component contracts and responsibilities; user research findings → fine-grained plan item (per the profile) scenarios and pain points; API documentation → integration acceptance criteria.

diagram [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: architecture diagrams, entity-relationship diagrams, sequence diagrams, flowcharts, state machines; informs the layered structure and integration points (layer count per the profile). Use cases: system architecture diagrams → the layered structure and component boundaries; entity-relationship diagrams → domain model and data structures; sequence diagrams → fine-grained plan item (per the profile) when/then steps and integration points; state machine diagrams → component behavior and state transitions.

audio [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: user interviews, voice notes, recorded requirements sessions; informs fine-grained plan item (per the profile) scenarios and pain points. Use cases: user interview recordings → extracting pain points and requirements; stakeholder requirement sessions → coarse plan artifact (per the profile) scope and priorities; voice memos → context and clarifications; accessibility testing feedback → accessibility harness criteria.

video [allowed extensions per the profile's appendix-type list]: screen recordings, demos, walkthroughs, user testing sessions; informs feature parity and reproduce steps. Use cases: demo of existing system behavior → feature parity requirements; user testing sessions → pain points and interaction patterns; tutorial videos → understanding complex workflows; screen recordings of bugs → fine-grained plan item (per the profile) reproduce steps.
avoid: Appendix filenames lacking the artifact-name and type segments.
Inventing a type outside the six (e.g. treating 'screenshot' as its own type — a screenshot of a UI is a mockup).
core.why: A fixed appendix taxonomy lets the planner recognize supplementary content, choose the right multimodal reading strategy, and map each artifact to the planner output it enriches.
evidence: Every appendix filename carries a type segment that is one of the six recognized types (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video), and its extension is in that type's allowed extension list from the profile.
verification: The allowed appendix type set is closed — exactly the six recognized types (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video); a filename type segment naming anything else must be flagged.

For every appendix file, the extension must be in the allowed extension list (per the profile's appendix-type lists) of the type carried in the filename's type segment; extensions are compared case-insensitively.
When an extension is allowed for more than one type, the type is taken from the filename's type segment, not inferred from the extension.
The check flags appendix filenames that lack the required name segments (artifact-name, type) or carry an unrecognized type segment.
Scope: only files that are appendices of plan artifacts; image assets, source assets or test fixtures elsewhere in the tree that are not attached to planner outputs are not covered by this check.

doesNotFire: An image asset is added to the source tree that is not an appendix of a plan artifact.

proposedKeys.meaning: The recognized appendix types of the stack's planner and, for each type, the file extensions allowed for appendix files of that type.
proposedKeys.bunValue: mockup: PNG, JPG, JPEG, SVG, GIF; spreadsheet: XLSX, CSV, TSV; document: PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT; diagram: PNG, SVG, MERMAID, DRAWIO; audio: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG; video: MP4, MOV, WEBM, AVI
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> is parametrized only over source/unit_test/acceptance_test/e2e_test/markup/plan_artifact/config file kinds; appendix files are supplementary artifacts attached to plan artifacts and keyed by appendix type, which no existing suffix key covers.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's plan-decomposition levels with their local names: which local kind is the coarse plan artifact (the bounded product slice carrying description and scope) and which is the fine-grained plan item (carrying when/must/then statements, scenarios, steps and reproduce steps).
proposedKeys.bunValue: coarse plan artifact -> wagon; fine-grained plan item -> WMBT
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.<role>.kinds lists a role's concrete kinds but is a flat list: it neither orders kinds by decomposition level nor binds each level's planning concerns (description/scope vs when/must/then statements, scenarios, steps, reproduce steps) to its kind name, so wagon-target vs WMBT-target guidance cannot be reconstructed from it.

proposedKeys.meaning: The number of dependency-ordered layer roles in the stack's layered structure, for guidance that refers to the structure by count.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.layers is the ordered list of layer-role local names, which bun.json does not state; the only layered-structure datum in this rule is the count, so it needs its own key rather than overloading roles.layers with a count or a descriptive phrase.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely method-level rather than stack-level. The six-type appendix taxonomy and the planning idioms it references (when/must/then statements, when/then steps, acceptance given/when sections, harness selection) are planner-method knowledge and stay verbatim in the core. Three things are stack/file data the core may not name: (1) the per-type file extension lists, moved to the proposed suffix.appendix_types key; (2) the plan-decomposition level names — the coarse plan artifact and fine-grained plan item that the per-type guidance targets — restored through the proposed roles.plan_artifact.levels key so the Bun realization instantiates wagon vs WMBT targets exactly; (3) the size of the layered structure ('4-layer'), carried by the proposed roles.layers.count because bun.json states no layer-role list, so roles.layers itself is not used. Concrete worked examples and counter-examples (evidence[1], the filenames in avoid[0], avoid[1], verifier_detail[7]) are not repeated in the core; bun.json remains the reference example. The core refers to 'the filename's type segment' without spelling out the concrete naming-pattern syntax, which belongs to the companion naming rule. Activation fact notes (contextual-signal caveat, planner-appendix-only meaningfulness) are preserved through the fires/doesNotFire framing and the check's scope in verification, since the neutral fact schema carries no note field.
